t: This is numbers 17 to 21 Portland Place, part of the broad, formal street running up toward Regent's Park. Alexander Macmillan died here in 1896. Born in Irvine, in Scotland, to a family of crofters from the Isle of Arran, he cofounded Macmillan Publishers in 1843 with his brother Daniel. The firm began in Covent Garden. So a publishing house that started small ended with one of its founders living, and dying, on one of London's grandest streets.
